decoderDiagnosticPolicies.reason: The decoder compares complete row bytes and keeps one copy of a byte-identical repeated row; the repeats carry no additional fact (4,186 keyword rows and 19 leader rows in the 2026-09-28 export).
Empty wargear and faction-keyword placeholder rows carry no game fact and are excluded by the decoder.

classificationPolicies.reason: Datasheets whose Wahapedia source is an 11th-edition publication (Source.csv edition 11) belong to the current rules context.
Warhammer Legends faction packs are kept in a separate Legends context that an army must opt into, matching the AoS Reminders allowsLegends overlay.

Forge World datasheets are offered by default in the current context (product decision, 2026-09-30). Official 11th-edition faction packs publish them alongside the main datasheets in separate Imperial Armour sections (for example the Imperial Knights faction pack contents list Imperial Armour Datasheets after the main datasheets). Each datasheet keeps its forge-world classification for provenance.

Deathwatch and Death Korps of Krieg datasheets cite only 10th-edition publications, and the 11th-edition downloads observed on 2026-09-30 carry no Deathwatch faction pack. They stay out of every 11th-edition context until official 11th-edition material covers them.

linkDispositions.reason: Child rows (288 unit-to-stratagem links plus wargear, keyword, model and ability rows) whose datasheet Wahapedia no longer publishes in Datasheets.csv. Without the parent datasheet they are unreachable and carry no selectable fact, so they are excluded rather than attached to a guessed unit.

Model, keyword, composition, wargear and ability rows for four generic Chaos Daemons templates (Greater Daemon, Lesser Daemons, Abomination, Daemonic Beasts) that have no Datasheets.csv record. They are not selectable datasheets and are excluded.

Nine unit-to-stratagem association rows (Battleline Space Marine squads) point at stratagem 000010677006, which Stratagems.csv does not publish. The association rows carry no rule text of their own and are excluded.

Tormentbringer has two leader rows; the other already targets Hellflayers. The official Chaos Daemons faction pack lists Hellflayers as the only unit Tormentbringer can join, so the row pointing at an unpublished datasheet is excluded.

officialEvidence.quote: LEADER This model can be attached to the following unit: ■ Hellflayers

linkDispositions.reason: Six Aeldari rows (Star Engines, Flitting Shadows, Sudden Strike, Fade Back, Swift as the Wind, Opportunity Seized) point at an 'Army Rules' detachment Detachments.csv does not publish, and carry no CP cost or stratagem type. They are Agile Manoeuvres of the Battle Focus army rule, not detachment stratagems: the official Aeldari faction pack amends 'Agile Manoeuvres, Star Engines' under ARMY RULES and describes the Fade Back Agile Manoeuvre as spending a Battle Focus token. They are retained as faction army rules. The pack names two of the six directly; the other four share the same army-rule rows.

officialEvidence.quote: ARMY RULES Agile Manoeuvres, Star Engines
This unit can perform the Fade Back Agile Manoeuvre without spending a Battle Focus token

timingOverrides.reason: Wahapedia prints Damaged as Core Rules 24.39, a standing modifier while a model’s remaining wounds are at or below a threshold. Neither the Core Rules nor the Universal Rules Updates candidate documents print 24.39, so this relies on the Wahapedia text until an official source is pinned.

33 rules whose Wahapedia text states a standing effect with no window of its own: weapon and unit abilities (Root-carved Weapons, Paired Krumpas), keyword-subject grants and eligibilities (Questing Tendrils, Yriel's Own, Interlocking Tactics), round-gated modifiers (Patient Hunter, Killing Blow 'During the first, second and third battle rounds'), and limits on other rules (Unstable Energies, Sacred Rites, Valour's Reward, Extremis Sanction). Brood Brothers and Wretched Thralls also permit units at muster, but each carries a standing in-game effect, so they stay always active.

ignoredRules.reason: 15 rules that only decide what an army may include or which keywords units carry at muster (Cult of the Dark Gods, Assigned Agents, Titanicus Traitoris, The Ravenwing, The Deathwing, Deathwatch, Corsairs and Travelling Players, retinue allowances, chapter Restrictions). Nothing to remind during a game.

Records with no playable rule of their own: the Sagas introduction ('Each Detachment rule in this book includes a Saga'), the Orks Special Move Types definitions that other rules invoke (like the excluded core move types), two FORTIFICATION assembly notes ('Both parts ... treated as a single model'), and the TL-4Ø9 enhancement, whose Wahapedia text is empty.

Wahapedia files 30 Core Rules move, shoot and fight types (Normal Move, Advance Move, Charge Move, Pile-in Move, Normal Shooting, Assault Shooting and similar) in Stratagems.csv with type 'Movement Ability' or 'Shooting Ability'. They are how every unit acts, not stratagems or optional rules, so they are not reminders.

11 unscoped stratagems typed 'Core – …' (Go To Ground, Tank Shock, Grenade, and 10th-edition copies of other core stratagems). The official 11th-edition Core Rules prints exactly ten core stratagems (15.02-15.12, 15.09 being Snap Shooting), which Wahapedia carries as the ten rows typed 'Core Stratagem'; Go To Ground, Tank Shock, and Grenade are not among them. These rows are not 11th-edition core stratagems.
5 unscoped stratagems typed 'Boarding Actions – …' belong to the Boarding Actions game mode, not matched play.
9 unscoped stratagems typed 'Challenger – …' come from mission-pack Challenger cards, which are drawn during a game rather than available to every army; they are not core stratagems.

3 unscoped copies of New Orders typed 'Core Stratagem – Strategic Ploy Stratagem'. New Orders is not among the ten core stratagems the official Core Rules prints (15.02-15.12), so these copies are not offered to every army.
8 Designer's Notes filed as abilities: clarifications, token-tracking advice and points commentary that explain another rule rather than grant one, so they are not reminders.
